subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should OpenClaw adopt Gateway-owned cron declarations and durable scheduler provenance as part of the permanent Claw package lifecycle once deletion is retry-safe and live proof is supplied?
rationale: The branch creates persistent state and lets package declarations create long-lived Gateway execution, while also broadening ordinary agent deletion; implementation correctness cannot determine whether that compatibility and security contract should become supported product behavior.

options.title: Approve after durability fix
options.body: Accept the canonical Gateway ownership model after post-commit deletion becomes resumable, focused upgrade tests are added, live proof is supplied, and the RFC is accepted.

options.title: Narrow the initial lifecycle
options.body: Defer cron declaration installation and provenance while landing only the already-approved Claw lifecycle surfaces.

options.title: Continue RFC incubation
options.body: Keep this stacked draft open without landing until the broader Claws product and upgrade contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve after durability fix
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical Gateway ownership model after post-commit deletion becomes resumable, focused upgrade tests are added, live proof is supplied, and the RFC is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the detailed owner-boundary and failure-recovery direction already incorporated into this branch and the linked RFC revision.
